hypotheses.justification: The proof uses hT_compact only once, as the argument it passes to `abs_eigenvector_of_top_eigenvector`. That lemma names the binder `_hT_compact` and its proof never uses it. The proof relies only on positivity preservation (via `abs_inner_le_inner_abs`), the bound `hlam₀_top`, self-adjointness (via `IsSelfAdjoint.eq_smul_self_of_isLocalExtrOn`) and norm facts. The other lemmas called, `ground_state_strictly_positive` and `IsPositivityImproving'.toPreserving`, take no compactness argument. The statement therefore holds for any bounded self-adjoint positivity-improving T: T|f| = λ₀|f|, so g = |f| - f ≥ 0 also satisfies T g = λ₀ g. If g = 0, f is nonnegative and nonzero, hence > 0 a.e. Otherwise g > 0 a.e., which forces f < 0 a.e. The case f = 0 is already excluded by hf_ne. To remove the hypothesis, inline the proof of `abs_eigenvector_of_top_eigenvector` (or drop its unused argument); nothing else in the proof changes.
